title: English Sentence Structure & Word Order Practice Questions
description: 80 practice questions categorized by core grammar rules from the study guide.

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'reads / she / books'
questions.explanation: English simple statements follow Subject (She) + Verb (reads) + Object (books).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'the project / finished / the team'
questions.explanation: Subject (The team) + Verb (finished) + Object (the project).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'a laptop / bought / Alex'
questions.explanation: Subject (Alex) + Verb (bought) + Object (a laptop).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'coffee / drinks / manager / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The manager) + Verb (drinks) + Object (coffee).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'an email / sent / supervisor / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The supervisor) + Verb (sent) + Object (an email).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'a report / wrote / candidate / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The candidate) + Verb (wrote) + Object (a report).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'delicious food / cooks / chef / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The chef) + Verb (cooks) + Object (delicious food).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'the code / reviewed / developer / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The developer) + Verb (reviewed) + Object (the code).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'new skills / learned / students / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The students) + Verb (learned) + Object (new skills).

questions.prompt: Reorder the words to form a correct SVO sentence: 'the document / signed / director / the'
questions.explanation: Subject (The director) + Verb (signed) + Object (the document).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct adjective order:
options: a beautiful small old round brown French wooden table
a French wooden round old small brown beautiful table
a small beautiful round brown old wooden French table
a wooden French brown round old small beautiful table
questions.correct_answer: a beautiful small old round brown French wooden table
questions.explanation: The correct order is Opinion (beautiful) -> Size (small) -> Age (old) -> Shape (round) -> Color (brown) -> Origin (French) -> Material (wooden) + Noun.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly places the adjective?
questions.explanation: Adjectives come before the noun they describe in English.

options: They discussed an important strategic decision.

They discussed an strategic decision important.
They discussed a strategic decision important.
questions.correct_answer: They discussed an important strategic decision.
questions.explanation: Opinion/quality adjectives come before modifying nouns/types.

questions.explanation: Opinion (valuable) -> Age (ancient) -> Material (gold) + Noun.

questions.prompt: Which option is correct?
options: We watched an exciting new action movie.

questions.prompt: Select the correct sentence:

He drives a German fast modern sports car.
He drives a sports fast German modern car.
He drives a modern sports German fast car.
questions.correct_answer: He drives a fast modern German sports car.
questions.explanation: Opinion/Quality (fast) -> Age (modern) -> Origin (German) -> Purpose (sports) + Noun.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The company introduced an innovative software tool.
The company introduced a tool software innovative.
The company introduced an software tool innovative.
The company introduced a software tool innovative.
questions.correct_answer: The company introduced an innovative software tool.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'innovative' comes before the noun phrase 'software tool'.

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence with correct adverb placement:
options: Carefully she reads the report direct.
questions.explanation: Do not place an adverb between a verb (reads) and its direct object (the report).

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly places the frequency adverb?
options: She travels for work often always.
questions.explanation: Frequency adverbs usually go in mid-position, before the main verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with 'to be':
questions.explanation: Mid-position adverbs go AFTER the verb 'to be'.

questions.prompt: Where does the adverb go in this sentence? 'He has ___ submitted the application.'
questions.explanation: Mid-position adverbs go between the auxiliary verb (has) and main verb (submitted).

questions.prompt: Which sentence is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Never separate the verb from its direct object with an adverb.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence with a front-position adverb of time:
options: She finished the report yesterday carefully yesterday.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of time can go at the front for emphasis.

questions.prompt: Which modifier placement is correct?
questions.explanation: Adverbs modifying adjectives must go directly before the adjective.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct sentence:
options: They worked diligently on the assignment.
They worked on the assignment diligently on.
questions.correct_answer: They worked diligently on the assignment.
questions.explanation: Manner adverbs like 'diligently' modify the verb and fit naturally after the verb or clause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'never' correctly?
options: He is never late for meetings.
He never is late for meetings.
He late is never for meetings.
Never he is late for meetings.
questions.correct_answer: He is never late for meetings.
questions.explanation: 'Never' comes after the verb 'to be'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option:
options: The flight was delayed unfortunately flight.
questions.explanation: Attitude adverbs like 'Unfortunately' can stand at the beginning of a clause.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct order of place and time at the end of a sentence:
options: We met at the office yesterday.
We met yesterday at the office.
We yesterday met at the office.
At the office yesterday we met.
questions.correct_answer: We met at the office yesterday.
questions.explanation: The default sequence at the end of a sentence is Place (at the office) -> Time (yesterday).

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly arranges place and time?
options: She will present the project in Port-au-Prince next week.
She will present the project next week in Port-au-Prince.
She next week will present the project in Port-au-Prince.
In Port-au-Prince next week she will present the project.
questions.correct_answer: She will present the project in Port-au-Prince next week.
questions.explanation: Standard neutral order is Place (in Port-au-Prince) before Time (next week).

questions.prompt: How can you move time to the front for emphasis?
options: Yesterday, we met at the office.
At the office, yesterday we met.
Met we at the office yesterday.
We at the office met yesterday.
questions.correct_answer: Yesterday, we met at the office.
questions.explanation: Time expressions can be placed at the very front followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: Select the correct sentence:
options: They arrived at the airport at 8:00 AM.
They arrived at 8:00 AM at the airport.
They at 8:00 AM arrived at the airport.
At 8:00 AM at the airport they arrived.
questions.correct_answer: They arrived at the airport at 8:00 AM.
questions.explanation: Place (at the airport) comes before Time (at 8:00 AM).

questions.prompt: Which sentence is most natural in neutral English?
options: We will have a meeting in Pétionville tomorrow.
We will have a meeting tomorrow in Pétionville.
We will have tomorrow a meeting in Pétionville.
We tomorrow will have a meeting in Pétionville.
questions.correct_answer: We will have a meeting in Pétionville tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Place (in Pétionville) precedes Time (tomorrow).

questions.prompt: Identify the grammatically preferred sentence:
options: The conference will take place at the hotel on Monday.
The conference will take place on Monday at the hotel.
The conference on Monday will take place at the hotel.
On Monday at the hotel the conference will take place.
questions.correct_answer: The conference will take place at the hotel on Monday.
questions.explanation: Place (at the hotel) -> Time (on Monday).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct structure:
options: He signed the contract in Saint-Marc last month.
He signed the contract last month in Saint-Marc.
He last month signed the contract in Saint-Marc.
In Saint-Marc last month signed he the contract.
questions.correct_answer: He signed the contract in Saint-Marc last month.
questions.explanation: Place (in Saint-Marc) comes before Time (last month).

questions.prompt: Fix the word order: 'She attended a workshop last night in Cap-Haïtien.'
options: She attended a workshop in Cap-Haïtien last night.
She attended last night a workshop in Cap-Haïtien.
She in Cap-Haïtien attended a workshop last night.
Last night in Cap-Haïtien attended she a workshop.
questions.correct_answer: She attended a workshop in Cap-Haïtien last night.
questions.explanation: Place (in Cap-Haïtien) should precede Time (last night).

questions.prompt: Select the correct alternative:
options: Last week, they launched the initiative in Jacmel.
They launched last week the initiative in Jacmel.
They in Jacmel launched the initiative last week.
In Jacmel last week launched they the initiative.
questions.correct_answer: Last week, they launched the initiative in Jacmel.
questions.explanation: Time can be at the front, with place following the object.

questions.prompt: Which option follows the Place -> Time rule?
options: The team completed the audit at headquarters on Friday.
The team completed the audit on Friday at headquarters.
The team on Friday completed the audit at headquarters.
At headquarters on Friday completed the team the audit.
questions.correct_answer: The team completed the audit at headquarters on Friday.
questions.explanation: Place (at headquarters) comes before Time (on Friday).

questions.prompt: Convert to negative: 'I understand the lesson.'
options: I do not understand the lesson.
I am not understand the lesson.
questions.correct_answer: I do not understand the lesson.
questions.explanation: Negatives require Subject + auxiliary (do) + not + main verb (understand).

questions.prompt: Convert to negative: 'She has finished her assignment.'
options: She has not finished her assignment.
She does not finished her assignment.
She is not finished her assignment.
questions.correct_answer: She has not finished her assignment.
questions.explanation: Auxiliary (has) + not + past participle (finished).

questions.prompt: Convert to negative: 'They can attend the meeting.'
options: They do not can attend the meeting.
They can attend not the meeting.
They are not attend the meeting.
questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary (can) + not + base verb (attend).

questions.prompt: Convert to negative: 'He is ready.'
questions.explanation: With 'to be' as the main verb, place 'not' directly after 'is'.

questions.prompt: Which negative sentence has correct adverb placement?
questions.explanation: In negatives, adverbs like 'often' usually go after 'not' and before the main verb.

questions.prompt: Convert to negative: 'They were at home.'
options: They did not were at home.
questions.explanation: 'To be' in past tense takes 'not' directly after 'were'.

questions.prompt: Select the correct negative sentence:
options: The team does not have enough time.
The team has not enough time.
The team not does have enough time.
The team does have not enough time.
questions.correct_answer: The team does not have enough time.
questions.explanation: Present simple main verb 'have' uses auxiliary 'does not have' in modern English.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is negative and grammatically correct?
options: We did not see any errors in the report.
We saw not any errors in the report.
We did see not any errors in the report.
We not did see any errors in the report.
questions.correct_answer: We did not see any errors in the report.
questions.explanation: Subject (We) + auxiliary (did) + not + verb (see).

questions.prompt: Convert to negative: 'He will accept the proposal.'
options: He will not accept the proposal.

He will accept not the proposal.
He is not accept the proposal.
questions.correct_answer: He will not accept the proposal.
questions.explanation: Modal (will) + not + main verb (accept).

questions.prompt: Convert to a Yes/No question: 'You understand the lesson.'
questions.explanation: Yes/No questions in present simple use Auxiliary (Do) + Subject (you) + Verb (understand).

questions.prompt: Convert to a Yes/No question: 'She has submitted the report.'
options: Does she have submitted the report?
questions.explanation: Invert the auxiliary verb (Has) and the subject (she).

questions.prompt: Convert to a Yes/No question: 'They can join the meeting.'
options: Do they can join the meeting?
questions.explanation: Invert the modal verb (Can) and subject (they).

questions.prompt: Form a Wh- question asking for place: 'You work (where)'
questions.explanation: Wh-word (Where) + Auxiliary (do) + Subject (you) + Verb (work).

questions.prompt: Form a Wh- question: 'She has studied (what)'
questions.explanation: Wh-word (What) + Auxiliary (has) + Subject (she) + Verb (studied).

questions.prompt: Form a question where the Wh-word is the subject: '(Who) called you?'
questions.explanation: When the Wh-word is the subject of the sentence, do not invert or use auxiliary 'do'.
